title: Sandboxed adopter codelab sprint notes (local harness + failure injection)
content:
Context and intent:
This is a working sprint note for a compact, instructor-led codelab aimed at internal adopters (SEs, solutions eng, early customers) to: onboard to Redwood SDKs, show production-minded patterns (prefix caching, streaming, retry/backoff), and exercise resilience under realistic infra noise via a local sandboxed harness with failure injection. The goal is a 60-90 minute guided lab that ends with a short take-home exercise and telemetry checks in Redwood Console.

Audience:
- Platform engineers and product engine integrators who will run Redwood in hosted/dedicated/private modes
- Solutions Engineers onboarding early customers
- Internal devs experimenting with embedding + streaming

High-level flow (60–90 mins):
1) Quick 5-min intros + objectives (what they will ship and what they will learn)
2) Environment bootstrap (10 min)
   - Install: minimal deps (Python 3.10+, node v18+ optional)
   - Local sandbox: docker-compose target that spins up a tiny proxy, a fake model backend (lightweight echo service), and a telemetry sink (file or local HTTP collector)
   - Provide small script: ./scripts/bootstrap-local.sh --creates keys, example config, sample prompts
3) Hands-on lab exercises (35–50 min)
   - Exercise A: Basic generation with SDK (5 min)
     - show API key usage, model selection, and deterministic seeding for repeatable demos
     - read tokens, stream responses to console
   - Exercise B: Cost-aware batching knob (10 min)
     - switch between single-request and batched-run modes using SDK flag --batch-window=0|50ms|200ms
     - measure tokens/sec and latency with included microbenchmark harness
   - Exercise C: Prefix/KV cache demo (10 min)
     - show expected latency delta when repeating prefixes, instrument KV hit-rate via telemetry collector
   - Exercise D: Failure injection & graceful fallback (10–15 min)
     - harness supports fault modes: delay, drop, corrupted-frames, backend-404
     - configure routing policy override: prefer low-latency host vs cheap host; force fallback to smaller model and observe response degradation and console alerts
     - teach safe retry patterns (idempotency, jittered backoff)
4) Observability & Eval (10 min)
   - Walk through console traces produced by the harness: per-token latency distribution, per-route cost breakdown, and an alert triggered by a regression test (example prompt set)
5) Take-home & stretch goals (5 min)
   - Add custom tool-calling handler for structured output
   - Replace the fake backend with an actual small open model container image

Design of the sandbox harness:
- Components: local-proxy, fake-model, telemetry-collector, failure-controller UI (tiny web page or CLI).
- Config: YAML config accepts per-route policy (priority list), simulated p50/p99 latencies, trace-sampling ratio, and KV cache TTL.
- Failure modes:
  - latency-spike: add N ms per-token
  - packet-loss: drop X% of streaming frames
  - error-inject: return 500 or 422 from backend
  - corrupted-output: flip characters or change token boundaries (used to demo evals / regression detection)

Instructor notes and scripting:
- Pre-check: ensure participants have docker + network access. Provide a fallback cloud-hosted sandbox for restricted laptops.
- Demo script (short):
  - step 1: ./scripts/bootstrap-local.sh
  - step 2: python examples/generate_demo.py --model redwood-small --stream
  - step 3: ./scripts/failure-controller --mode latency-spike --p50 300 --window 30s
  - step 4: open telemetry viewer at http://localhost:8081/trace/last
- Time-box checkpoints: keep exercises tight; if group falls behind, skip batching exercise and go to failure injection for higher impact.

Pedagogical touches (what makes this different):
- Emphasize operational tradeoffs (latency vs cost) with hands-on knobs instead of just slides.
- Use realistic noise patterns rather than synthetic, constant delays (bursts, correlated failures).
- Include a tiny eval harness that runs a curated prompt set after each change and surfaces a regression score (so participants see how quantization/fallback affects quality).
- Encourage participants to instrument their local apps with same metrics Redwood Console expects (token_count, decode_latency, kv_hit).

Open questions / TODOs (working):
- Decide canonical small model image to recommend for local replaceable backend (options: llama2-7b-compat trimmed image vs tiny open transformer). Needs security check for redistribution. (owner: Priya)
- Telemetry viewer: simple file/JS viewer is OK for lab, but can we reuse a pared-down Console snapshot API to make traces look identical? Ask infra for read-only console token. (owner: Diego)
- Licensing: check if we can publish the lab sample prompt set externally; some prompts are customer-derived and need redaction. (owner: Maya)
- Time target: confirm 60 vs 90 minute variants; propose two scripts: fast-track (60m) and deep-dive (90m)

Checklist for authoring repository (minimum viable):
- [ ] scripts/bootstrap-local.sh (create minimal .env, start docker compose)
- [ ] examples/generate_demo.py and README with step-by-step
- [ ] failure-controller with modes: latency-spike, drop, corrupt, 404
- [ ] telemetry-collector that writes JSON lines + tiny web UI to visualise last N requests
- [ ] sample prompts (10) and an eval harness that calculates a simple similarity/regression score
- [ ] instructor script with timing and backup plan for restricted laptops

Quick debugging heuristics for instructors:
- If docker compose fails: check ports 8080–8085 conflict, suggest change in .env or run single-container mode
- If streaming stalls: run tcpdump to see if frames are sent; check that local proxy isn't buffering chunked responses
- If telemetry empty: confirm trace-sampling ratio is not zero in config and that collector endpoint is reachable

Suggested follow-ups after pilot run:
- Collate common participant questions and fold into FAQ doc
- Create a 20-minute recorded version of the lab for asynchronous onboarding
- Add a short section mapping each exercise to product docs (SDK refs, Console metrics, Dedicated config)

Notes to self:
- Keep wording non-Redwood-specific enough to reuse for partners, but include concrete Redwood SDK snippets as examples
- Keep slides to a single 7-slide deck for orientation + 2 live-demos; the rest should be hands-on

Last edits: 2025-02-11 by Maya Singh
summary: Sprint notes for a hands-on, sandboxed codelab to teach SDK usage, batching/caching knobs, and failure-injection for observability and resilience. Includes flow, harness design, instructor script, checklist, and open questions.
